children.text: kutaḥ khalvidaṃ kṣīyate yena śarīrāṇi śīryanta ityāha abhighātādityādi ||
children.translated_text: He states, beginning with 'from injury,' the answer to the question: 'From what, indeed, does this waste away, whereby bodies fall apart?'
'From wasting' means from the diminution of the <s>dhātu</s>s through excessive sexual activity and the like.

children.text: nanvevaṃ cettattvaṃ kathaṃ tarhyebhirhetubhirupataptāḥ sarvakriyāsvasamarthā apyāturāḥ sadyo na mriyanta ityāśaṅkyāha hītyādi ||
children.translated_text: If this is so, one may object, then how is it that patients afflicted by these causes, though incapable of all actions, do not die immediately? Anticipating this doubt, he says the passage beginning with 'for.'
This follows the rule that every statement is to be read with restriction.
The meaning is: from these causes alone, namely injury and the rest.

children.text: tejaḥ sarvadhātūnāṃ dīpto'ṃśa oja iti niṣkarṣaḥ vāyunā cālitaṃ sat dhātugrahaṇaniḥsṛtaṃ dhātavo gṛhyanta ebhiriti dhātugrahaṇāni vakṣyamāṇāni srotāṃsi tebhyo niḥsṛtaṃ nirgataṃ bhavati tasmāddehino visraṃsayati sarvebhya eva karmabhyo bahiṣkaroti natu sadyo mārayatīti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is that <s>ojas</s> is the bright essence of all the <s>dhātu</s>s. When it has been set in motion by <s>vāyu</s>, it issues from the <s>dhātugrahaṇa</s>s, that is, the channels to be described, so called because the <s>dhātu</s>s are held by them. Having gone out from them, it causes the embodied being to collapse; it excludes him from all actions, but does not kill him immediately. This is the purport.

children.text: etenaujasaḥ kṣaye mriyate mūlasthānātpracyāvite tu sarvakarmaṇāmatipatito bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this it is stated that when <s>ojas</s> is depleted one dies, but when it is displaced from its root-place, one becomes fallen away from all action.

children.text: vakṣyati ca kriyāsaṃnirodhaśca visraṃse iti hārāṇacandraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Hārāṇacandra</s> will also say: 'There is cessation of activity when there is displacement.'

children.text: dhātavo gṛhyante yaistāni dhātugrahaṇāni srotāṃsi ojovāhīni yaduktam ojovahā vidhamyante śarīre'smin samantataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Those by which the <s>dhātu</s>s are held are the <s>dhātugrahaṇa</s>s, the channels that carry <s>ojas</s>. As has been said: 'The <s>ojovahā</s>s are diffused everywhere in this body.'

children.text: kiṃvā dhātugrahaṇasrotaḥsthānatayā dhātugrahaṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ tato niḥsṛtaṃ dhamanībhireva kiṃvā niṣṭhitam iti pāṭhaḥ tadā ojovāhisrotaḥsu hṛdi sthitamityarthaḥ iti cakraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, since the heart is the location of the channel that holds the <s>dhātu</s>s, <s>dhātugrahaṇa</s> means the heart; from that it has gone out through the arteries alone. Alternatively, if the reading is 'niṣṭhitam,' then the meaning is that it is situated in the <s>ojovāhī</s> channels, in the heart. So says <s>Cakra</s>.
'Bimba' is said to be the perforated threefold bone.
